# Adaptive Gaussian cap preservation and an actual critical cover that freezes it

This is a bounded capability/obstruction result for base-only stochastic localization. It extends the finite Gaussian identities, not the continuous-fiber needle localization theorem. The archived `candidate f7afca279c65bd1a` already blocks preservation of arbitrary fiber masses and bad-cap inequalities under a different continuous reduction; Section 5 below distinguishes that earlier obstruction.

## 1. Adaptive covariance and exact cap martingales

Fix actual uniform conditional fiber laws and positive original base probabilities pi_z on a finite P spanning its inherited real base space R^n. Let A_t be an adapted symmetric positive semidefinite matrix process, locally integrable in time, and define

    Q_t=integral_0^t A_s ds,
    p_z(t)=pi_z exp(a_t.z-z^T Q_t z/2)/Z_t,
    m_t=sum_z p_z(t) z,
    da_t=A_t m_t dt+A_t^(1/2)dW_t.                     (1)

Assume the displayed continuous process exists with finite a_t,Q_t on each finite localized time interval. No separate existence theorem for a discontinuous chosen feedback A(p) is asserted. Degenerate PSD matrices are permitted.

Itô's formula gives exactly

    dp_z=p_z(z-m_t)^T A_t^(1/2)dW_t.                   (2)

The quadratic base penalty cancels the unnormalized quadratic variation; normalization cancels the remaining A_t m_t drift. Stochastic variation of A does not add a term to Q, which is of finite variation. Because p_z is bounded between zero and one, these local martingales are true bounded martingales after the usual finite-time localization and limit.

For a FIXED actual closed cap H_j let

    g_j(z)=|K_z intersect H_j|/|K_z|,
    G_j(t)=sum_z p_z(t)g_j(z),
    c_j(p)=Cov_p(g_j(z),z)=sum_z p_z g_j(z)(z-m).

Its exact dynamics and joint brackets are

    dG_j=c_j(p_t)^T A_t^(1/2)dW_t,
    d<G_i,G_j>_t=c_i(p_t)^T A_t c_j(p_t) dt.            (3)

All fiber boundary statuses, including pure-base closed caps, are encoded in the fixed fractions g_j. The formulas require no smoothness of a fiber or a cap trace.

## 2. Exact simultaneous preservation condition

For a finite fixed menu, the following are equivalent along an existing process (1), up to dt times probability null sets:

    every G_j is pathwise constant;
    c_j(p_t)^T A_t c_j(p_t)=0 for every j;
    A_t c_j(p_t)=0 for every j;
    range(A_t) is contained in span{c_j(p_t)}^perp.       (4)

The first equivalence follows because a continuous local martingale is constant exactly when its quadratic variation is zero. The PSD property gives equivalence of the next two statements. This is an exact preservation condition, not merely vanishing of an expectation derivative.

If the vectors c_j span the base space, A_t must vanish. A rank-deficient span permits nonzero instantaneous PSD choices supported on its orthogonal complement, but a global construction must keep (4) true as the state changes and prove existence of its feedback process. Neither is automatic.

There is no escape by replacing equality with pathwise preservation of active upper bounds. If G_j(0)=q_j and G_j(t)<=q_j almost surely for all t, bounded martingality implies equality at every fixed t. Continuity gives pathwise constancy. Thus preserving all initially active cap inequalities is subject to exactly the same condition (4).

## 3. An actual sharp critical-cap cover with full-rank covariance

Take P={0,1}^n, n>=1, and the same d-simplex T at every base, d>=1. Write its barycentric coordinates as lambda_0,...,lambda_d. Let g be its centroid and gamma=Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. Original base weights are uniform, 1/N with N=2^n.

For each base vertex v define its exposing vector e_v=(2v_1-1,...,2v_n-1). For every j define the ACTUAL ambient halfspace

    H_(v,j)={lambda_j(X)+e_v.(z-v)>=1/(d+1)}.          (5)

At its own base this is the canonical simplex centroid cap of fraction gamma. At any other binary base, e_v.(z-v)<=-1 and lambda_j<=1, so the cap is empty there. Hence

    g_(v,j)(z)=gamma 1_(z=v),
    G_(v,j)(p)=gamma p_v,
    c_(v,j)(p)=gamma p_v(v-m).                         (6)

Every halfspace in (5) contains the actual mark (v,g). The d+1 caps of a base cover its entire simplex, since some barycentric coordinate is at least 1/(d+1). Thus the FULL finite menu covers every point of the actual mixed set. At the original prior every cap has mass gamma/N. These are actual critical caps: exposing-base isolation shows that the global mixed depth is exactly gamma/N and every fiber centroid is deepest.

For any strictly positive posterior p, the vectors v-m span R^n, since their pairwise differences span it. Therefore preserving the cap probabilities of this actual critical cover forces A=0. This holds at EVERY positive posterior, not only initially, so adaptation cannot move around a singular starting constraint matrix.

In fact n particular cap rows already suffice. Choose bases v_0=0, v_j=e_j for j=1,...,n-1, and one canonical cap at each. The determinant of the raw column matrix

    [-m, e_1-m, ..., e_(n-1)-m]

has absolute value m_n>0. Consequently the absolute covariance determinant is

    gamma^n m_n product_(j=0,...,n-1)p_(v_j)>0.         (7)

At the original prior it is gamma^n/(2 N^n). These n rows belong to the genuine covering menu (5); no artificial events or freely assigned fractions have been inserted.

All cap probabilities start at their active upper bound gamma/N. Requiring them never to exceed that bound therefore freezes every nontrivial adaptive Gaussian covariance by Section 2. The example is exactly sharp for OC, not a below-target counterexample. It proves that such preservation cannot be assumed even at a genuine full critical cover.

## 4. A strictly subtarget cap menu also freezes a base direction

The archived actual product P={0,1,2} with triangle fibers T has three caps

    H_j={lambda_j(X)-z>=1/3},       j=0,1,2.

Each captures only its canonical triangle cap at base zero. With the uniform prior its probability is 4/27, strictly below the n=1,d=2 target 2/9. Its base covariance is

    c_j=(4/9)(1/3)(0-1)=-4/27!=0.

Thus even one of these active inequalities forces scalar A=0 if it is required to remain below its original bound. All three together cover the zero fiber; they do NOT cover the whole mixed set. This distinction is essential and agrees with the archived scope.

The earlier note rules out changing the continuous conditional law to a needle while preserving those bounds and all fiber ratios. The present calculation is a different statement: even if every conditional law stays exactly uniform and only base Gaussian weights evolve, exact preservation of the same active small caps blocks the relevant stochastic direction.

## 5. What remains possible

Fixed-cap expectations are automatically conserved by (1), but individual sample paths need not retain the constraints. An expectation-only assertion therefore does not preserve an actual covering certificate. Conversely, a pathwise certificate can force all covariance to vanish, as above.

This does not rule out discarding redundant constraints, moving the caps, changing their allowed bounds, stopping and using additional original-measure information, or introducing another invariant. Those would require separate proofs. In particular none of the formulas says that an arbitrary selected bad menu admits a nontrivial covariance orthogonal to its cap covariances. The full-rank actual examples show why that missing rank condition cannot be silently imposed.

The cube-times-simplex example is already a sharp heavy-fiber case, so it does NOT block an algorithm that stops as soon as a valid heavy certificate is found. The following additions test precisely that repair.

## 6. Strictly nonheavy product calibration

Take instead P={-1,0,1}^n and the same simplex T at every base. Now N=3^n and k=2^n. Every original fiber has mass fraction 1/N<1/k, so the family is strictly nonheavy.

Choose n affinely independent corner vertices of the facet z_n=1: start with v_0=(1,...,1), and for j=1,...,n-1 flip coordinate j to -1 to obtain v_j. At each selected vertex use the d+1 halfspaces

    H_(v,j)={lambda_j(X)+v.(z-v)>=1/(d+1)}.            (8)

They again isolate the canonical simplex cap at their own vertex; every other ternary base has v.(z-v)<=-1. Their common ORIGINAL probability is

    q=Gamma_d/3^n < Gamma_d/2^n.                       (9)

Thus these are genuine active bounds at one common strictly subtarget budget q. Each selected group is the ordinary centroid critical circuit of its own fiber. It is not claimed to be globally critical in the mixed family.

For EVERY positive posterior, m_n<1. The determinant of the n raw covariance directions v_j-m has absolute value

    2^(n-1)(1-m_n)>0.

Multiplying by their nonzero Gamma_d p_(v_j) factors proves full covariance span. Consequently preserving these active cap bounds freezes all covariance, even though no original fiber is heavy. Each group covers its selected vertex fiber, but the menu leaves the other fibers uncovered. It is not a global small-cap cover.

This product does have an independently certified good center: at (0,g_T), every ambient cap contains g_T on a closed base halfspace of weight at least 1/2, by base reflection. Its continuous capture on each such fiber is at least Gamma_d. Hence original depth is at least Gamma_d/2>=Gamma_d/2^n. The example defeats a HEAVY-ONLY stopping repair; it does not defeat an algorithm able to detect this additional affine-centroid geometry.

## 7. Arbitrarily small full-rank cap menus exist for every full-rank family

There is a general reason that covariance rank of an arbitrary small-cap menu cannot itself supply new body geometry. Let P be any finite full-rank base in R^n, n>=1, with positive actual convex fibers and positive probabilities pi_z. Fix any alpha>0. Choose a facet F of conv(P) and n affinely independent vertices v_1,...,v_n on F. They are exposed vertices of conv(P). Choose

    0<q<min{alpha, pi_(v_1),...,pi_(v_n)}.

In fiber K_(v_i), continuity and strict monotonicity of a directional tail between its support extremes provide a proper cap of fraction kappa_i=q/pi_(v_i). Expose v_i in the base and multiply its exposing normal by a sufficiently large finite scalar. The resulting ACTUAL ambient halfspace H_i preserves this own cut and misses all other fibers strictly. Its capture vector and original mass are therefore

    g_i(z)=kappa_i 1_(z=v_i),       mu_original(H_i)=q. (10)

This construction uses bounded actual fibers, not independent formal capture assignments.

For every positive posterior, the mean m lies strictly on the interior side of the facet F. The n vectors v_i-m are linearly independent. Indeed, if sum t_i(v_i-m)=0 and s=sum t_i, applying a facet functional equal to b on F gives s(b-a.m)=0. Its factor b-a.m is positive, so s=0; affine independence of the v_i then forces every t_i=0. Thus

    Cov_p(g_i,z)=kappa_i p_(v_i)(v_i-m)

span the entire base space. Every nontrivial adaptive covariance is frozen if all the active bounds in (10) must remain satisfied pathwise.

In particular this full-rank menu can be manufactured for EVERY nonheavy actual family, with q arbitrarily below Gamma_d/k(P). It says nothing about its actual globally deepest marks and need not cover the mixed set. The n small budgets are active at their actual common value q; they are NOT active at a larger imposed common target alpha.

Therefore a statement that full span of such ARBITRARY small active caps implies a valid original center would add no hypothesis to the original general existence problem. It would be a theorem-strength re-expression, not a new consequence of rank. A meaningful selective-localization rule must restrict which actual caps may be retained—for example through a proved relation to a global critical cover—and must prove that the retained rank leaves a direction or yields an independently available deterministic certificate. No such global alternative is claimed here.
